message:
Merge pull request #292 from SovranBitcoin/fix/parallel-harness-devices

Let parallel agent runs share one Mac: own simulators, one native lease, phone dev links

Close the lease, reclaim and outage races the review found

The lease file was created empty and filled a moment later, so a second
process could read it as stale, delete it and take the lease too. It is now
written aside and linked into place, a stale lease is moved aside only if
it still names the dead holder, and the lease can be released early.

Reclaim now holds the lease throughout, skips Android emulator folders a
running emulator still uses, and leaves the shared simulators older
checkouts' unleased runs may be cloning from. Making a checkout's own
simulator takes the lease, and a story that simulator has already played
gets a fresh copy instead of being refused as a replayed wallet.

Outages expire by the current time rather than the catalog's, a route they
would empty keeps its candidates instead of refusing every task, and the
record is renamed into place and ignored if unreadable. dev-tunnel's --stop
accepts a branch name and its readiness probe times out.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Record the harness problems the device work leaves open

The upgrade gate that fails every app change on main, research failures
that end a task instead of amending it, bound runs that rebuild both
platforms every time, and Simulator.app showing harness simulators.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Tell workers and coordinators how to share devices, and keep results durable

Past runs booted shared simulators, opened Simulator.app and a windowed
emulator by hand, and fought over them across worktrees. Every brief now
says to look at the app only through the story runners (this checkout's own
windowless simulator, about 12 s a story), never to start devices or Metro
on 8081 directly, and to report a disk refusal rather than delete files.

A finished worker's result was lost when the task host restarted and the
run sat idle for 19 hours. Briefs now name a resultFile under the task's
state folder for a recovery copy, and the skill tells the coordinator to
check it rather than wait. The skill also checks the shared Mac before
intake and serves the published branch to the owner's phone.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Skip a provider that is out of quota when routing the next task

In the last runs Codex had hit its usage limit until a week later, yet 12 of
26 dispatches still went to it first: each ticket spent a dispatch and a
fallback rediscovering the same quota. A fallback now records the outage
(a quota covers the whole provider, other reasons one model) with an
assumed end, and model-policy leaves those candidates out of new routes
until then. A route left with no model fails at policy time, before intake.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Run each checkout's dev server behind its own tunnel, with a phone link

`bun run dev:tunnel` starts Metro on the first free port from 8082 behind
https://sovran-<branch>.ngrok.io, so many worktrees can serve at once.
`--detach` waits until the tunnel answers and prints
https://sovran-<branch>.ngrok.io/_expo/link?choice=expo-dev-client: Expo
redirects that into the installed dev client, so tapping it in a chat on a
phone opens this checkout's build. Checked through the tunnel with iPhone
and Android user agents, and in Safari on a simulator, which offered to
open it in Sovran.

This replaces the copy that lived only in ~/.local/bin/sovran-dev.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Give each checkout its own simulators and serialise native work

Story runs in two worktrees shared one prepared simulator and one set of
worker simulators by name, and each run deleted every worker before it
started, so parallel harness runs removed each other's devices mid-story.
Simulators are now named after their checkout. A single story plays on the
checkout's own simulator, made on first use and reused (about 12 s a story
after that), so nobody has to pick or boot one by hand.

Builds, multi-story runs, bound runs and Android stories take one lease for
the whole Mac and wait their turn, and refuse to start below 20 GB free,
pointing at `machine.ts reclaim`, which lists what runs left behind.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Merge pull request #291 from SovranBitcoin/feat/native-ui-gate

Let UI work pass full-send on story runs bound to a fresh build on iPhone and Android

Record that the testing coverage ledger fails its own contract on main

Two coverage-ledger tests fail on main at 82c8add85: a cited test was
deleted, and a NIP-05 scenario has no ledger entry. They fail this PR's
Tests and code-quality checks too; the branch changes neither.

Name the follow-ups F166 covers one by one

A range read as an id the ledger no longer has.

Record that the docs build fails on 22 dead links

This PR's CI fails the Docs build on the same 22 links as main at
82c8add85. Each links from the docs site to a file outside it, such as the
app's ADRs, the harness README or a skill.

Tell knip the controller runs bound.ts, and keep two harness names private

bound.ts is started by the full-send controller, not by a package script,
so knip took it for unused. NATIVE_RUNNER and NativeCheck are only used
in the files that define them.

Say why an iOS screen capture failed

Under heavy load a bound iOS run failed with only the simctl command line
as its reason, so a broken simulator and a slow machine looked the same.
A failed capture now carries simctl's exit code and what it wrote to
stderr, and a capture that runs out of time says so.

Say what the native story gate now does, and what F156 still needs

The harness README said UI tasks always stop incomplete. They now pass
through a sealed native requirement whose stories play on both platforms;
performance tasks still stop. F156 records the manual bound run that
passed on both platforms, the runner defects it exposed, and what is left:
a controller-driven pilot, two stories that start from saved states, and
performance evidence.

Pass the story id to the Android bound run, and say which builds get the larger heap

The Android run read the story file again for an id the caller already had.
The Gradle heap comment said bundled builds only; it applies to every e2e
Android build made here, and not to EAS builds.

Reach the Settings rows with until, and wait on the Developer mode toast itself

The history story's three Settings swipes now start on the page and swipe
until their row is in reach. On Android one stopped short of the end and
left the Terms row on the bottom edge, so the next swipe started there and
moved nothing. Each scrolling step gets 15 seconds for its swipes.

Turning on Mock Mode or Mock Offline in two more stories waited for a toast
to be logged as hidden. That toast comes from pressing the version two steps
earlier, so on a slow run it hid first and the step waited for nothing. They
now wait until the toast is gone from the screen.

Close the gaps an audit found in swiping until a control is in reach

- Swiping left or right, a card is in reach once it is wholly on screen.
  The band clear of a header and a tab bar applied to height alone, so a
  card off to the side passed at once, and a centred one beside it could
  never pass.
- An element taller than that band is in reach once it fills it, and one
  wholly on screen is in reach once the page stops moving at its end. Both
  used to spend all eight swipes and fail. Android swipes vary as well: a
  Settings swipe that once flung to the end stopped 392 points short.
- The step's deadline holds between swipes. It was only checked after them.
- A swipe on an element with no part on screen fails rather than starting at
  the edge of the glass, where Android may take it as the home gesture. The
  start point is kept on the glass like the end point.
- ADR 0033, the runner's header and the stories README now say that a swipe
  with `until` is the one bounded repeat, and that stories reach a control
  with it rather than a measured distance.

Swipe the wallet until View all is in the open, and wait on the toast itself

Swiping by a set distance left View all under the iOS header. The story
now swipes the wallet page until View all is clear of the bars.

Turning on Mock Mode waited for a toast to be logged as hidden, but that
toast comes from pressing the version two steps before. On a slow run it
hid before this step began, and the step waited for nothing. The step now
waits until the toast is gone from the screen.

Let a story swipe until a control is in the open

A swipe carries a page further on iOS than on Android: in the wallet a
0.15 swipe moved the page about 350 points on iOS and about 137 on
Android. No one distance put View all in reach on both; on iOS it ended
under the header, where the tap opened the mint list. A swipe step can
now name `until`: it swipes again, at most eight times, until that element
sits whole between a fifth and four fifths of the screen's height, clear
of a header and a tab bar.

The finger also goes down on the part of the swiped element that is on
screen. A long page's centre is often above or below the glass.

Give the e2e Android release build a 4 GB Gradle heap

Since a bundled build regenerates android/ with prebuild --clean, Gradle
runs with the 2 GB heap prebuild writes, and R8 ran out of it. The larger
heap is passed on the command line, so only these builds get it.

Scroll the wallet a little less before pressing View all

At 0.6 of the screen, iOS carried View all up under the floating wallet
header, and the tap opened the mint list. Android lays the wallet out
taller, so the same press needs View all above its tab bar. At 0.55 it
sits clear of both on both platforms.

Name an iOS bound run by its story id, and make it before the simulator

The run manifest only accepts plain names, so passing the story's path made
every bound iOS run fail before it played. The failure also came after the
simulator was created and outside the cleanup, so it left a booted
simulator behind. The run folder is now made first, named by the story id.

Close the second audit's gaps in the native story gate

- A bundled Android build regenerates android/ with prebuild --clean, as
  iOS already does. The folder is ignored by Git and by the native
  fingerprint, so an edit left in it would have reached the APK unseen.
- The runner guard covers host-side runner code and its configuration only.
  The app under test reports its own screen, so in-app e2e helpers are
  candidate code whose output the frames and video are checked against, and
  page registrations are data a new route has to add. Guarding them stopped
  ordinary UI work.
- A step picture must be a regular file, not a folder.
- `taps` is for a hidden control that needs several presses, never one
  that sends, publishes or deletes. The version row allows 1.5 seconds
  between presses, not 1.5 seconds in all, as an earlier message said.
- Stale comments corrected.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Let a story press a control several times as one action

Revealing the developer rows takes three presses of the app version inside
1.5 seconds. A bundled build keeps that real timing, and three separate
steps, each waiting for the screen to settle and taking its picture, can no
longer fit inside it. A tap step may now say `taps`: the runner presses
that many times back to back, with nothing between. The View all story uses
it, and checks that developer mode was actually turned on rather than only
that the version row is still there.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Close the gaps an audit found in the native story gate

- Android: payload.json hashes APK bytes while the stamp's hash also frames
  names and modes, so comparing them refused every run. Compare the
  installed APK with the built one; the fixture now writes distinct hashes.
- The runner guard missed files bound.ts loads or is configured by: the e2e
  schema, root scripts, bunfig, manifests, the lockfile, tsconfig and the
  app's e2e helpers. They are guarded now.
- Builds are always made afresh. The build folder is ignored by Git, so a
  stamp left there could vouch for any binary.
- UI work needs a sealed native requirement on both platforms, so stories
  are always judged by a story-oracle review.
- A simulator counts as removed only when simctl listed devices.
- A step picture must be a file in its own run folder.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Wait for an Android screen to stop moving before tapping it

Android stories had no screen-stillness check, so a tap could land while a
list was still flinging after a swipe; Android then spends the tap stopping
the scroll, and the Mock Mode switch never turned on. Android runs now use
the same fresh-capture watch as iOS, fed by adb screenshots. A recorder stop
that already failed is no longer reported a second time during cleanup.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Tap Android header buttons where they are drawn

The screen map placed every header control on Android just under the
safe-area inset, which is right for iOS, where the layout puts a header
above its page. On Android the header is laid out where it is drawn: the
inset guess put the wallet's drawer button about 30 points low, so a bound
story tapped beneath it, and an offline banner moves the header down too.
Android header controls now use their measured frame, corrected for the
viewport origin like the rest of the page.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Add a story that opens the whole history from the wallet's View all

It starts fresh, so a bound run can play it: Terms, Privacy and setup, then
Mock Mode for payments without spending anything, then View all under the
latest payments on the wallet, ending on the history page.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Let UI work pass full-send on bound story runs from both platforms

The controller stopped every UI task because no native result was tied to
the candidate. A native-stories check now seals stories and platforms. The
controller runs app/e2e/stories/bound.ts, which builds each bundled app,
plays every story on its own disposable simulator or emulator, and copies
the evidence into the task folder.

The controller judges that evidence itself. It needs exactly one run per
sealed story and platform for this invocation, the sealed story bytes, a
bundled build whose source fingerprint is the candidate's, an install
identical to the build, the app that answered being this run's, every step
passed with a picture, a video, an app log and the device removed. Each file
becomes receipt evidence, so reviewers must inspect every frame and video,
and a native requirement needs a story-oracle review citing the stories and
the inspection. A candidate that edits the runner is refused.

UI work without such a check on both platforms still stops; performance work
still always stops.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Record a video of every Android story run

ADR 0033 asks for one continuous video per story, and Android runs had
none. The iOS recorder's lifecycle now serves both platforms: a recorder
that exits before it is stopped, or finishes uncleanly, fails the run.
Android records with screenrecord from just before launch, stops it with an
interrupt sent on the device (interrupting the local adb client leaves an
unreadable file), then pulls the file into story.mp4. A story longer than
screenrecord's three-minute limit fails as a gap.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Merge pull request #290 from SovranBitcoin/feat/mint-details-instant

Open the mint page instantly, keep its stars and ring, and add a Details page
Record what the iPhone simulator showed of the mint page

Wait for the mint page's data before the store screenshot

Details shows on the mint page's first frame, so waiting for it no longer
means the page has loaded. The store screenshot recipe now also waits for the
reviews action, as the marketing recipe does, and its pin is updated for that
one read-only step.

Keep a mint's listed name when its own info leaves it blank

The mint page now opens before the mint's info arrives, showing the name the
list had. When that info came back with no name, the bridge replaced it with
the URL, so the title switched to an address a moment after opening. The
bridge now falls back to the listed name before the URL.

In the Details rows, a name that is only the address is left out, and counts
are written with separators (12,345) as the page writes them.

Record the device checks the mint page change still needs

F165 lists what tests could not show: the instant open from the Select Mint list, the stars and ring on the first frame, the Details modal stacked over the mint-flow modal, and the edited scenarios and stories, none of which ran on an iPhone or an Android phone. It links F65 and F156.

Wait for the mint page by its Details button in native tests

Six scenarios and three stories waited for, or left by, the footer's Close button, which is now Details. They wait for mint-info-details-open instead, and the story that closed the page now uses the flow header's close. The accepter's Reject keeps mint-info-close, so receive-cashu-unknown-mint-reject is unchanged.

Three of those scenarios are reviewed capture recipes. Their expanded steps differ from before only by that selector on both platforms, so their REVIEWED_STEPS pins are updated, and a capture test checks that none of their targets is blocked for a changed recipe and that each still has targets.

Replace the mint page's Close button with Details

The footer's Close repeated the header's close. In its place a Details button opens the shared Details modal, as the transaction pages do, with everything else known about the mint: what its NUT-06 info says (name, software, key, units, supported features by name, message, descriptions, contacts), how it has been running (status, audit result, success rate, timing, counts, auditor, 24-hour uptime, when audited), its reviews, its operator's Nostr identity, reputation and Vertex rank, and when each part was last read. Unknown values are left out.

The rows come from a pure builder, buildMintDetailsRows, and the modal gains four groups after the existing ones. The accepter flow keeps Reject and Accept, and Reject keeps its mint-info-close id. The long-description card is now "More about this mint", so only the button is called Details.

Keep a mint's stars and audit ring on screen from the first frame

The rating chart unmounted whenever no score was known and reviews were not loading, so a mint nobody had rated lost its stars. It now stays mounted in every state but a failed read with no score, and an opt-in empty state draws the stars with "No ratings yet" at the same height. The reviews screen does not opt in, so it still shows no chart for an unrated mint.

The ring around the icon faded in from nothing after the content mounted, and with no audit it drew a 50/50 green and red split that read as a score. It now draws on the first frame, as a plain track when the mint has not been audited.

Open a mint's page from the selector without waiting for its info

The three-dots button on a Select Mint row awaited buildMintReviewInfo, a NUT-06 read with a 3 s deadline plus balance and trust reads, before navigating. It now navigates at once with the row's name, icon, score and review count under the seed keys buildMintInfoHref uses, and the page's bridge fetches the rest after it opens, as every other entry point already does. buildMintReviewInfo stays for the review step.

Merge pull request #288 from SovranBitcoin/feat/offline-send-just-works

Offline send, payments edition, nearby payments, the app-style rebuild, native stories and the full-send harness (kept at 0.1.3)

Quote <store> in F72 so the docs build can parse it

VitePress read the bare placeholder as an unclosed element and stopped the build.

Let the harness suite run in a shallow CI checkout

The held-out cases read their sources from commits a depth-1 clone does not have, one of them only on PR #289's branch; copy those five files into harness/evaluations/sources. Three publisher and controller tests outran Bun's 5 s default on the Linux runner; give the harness suite 30 s per test.

Prune lint suppressions the branch no longer needs

ESLint exits 2 when a recorded suppression no longer matches, which would fail the lint job. Only obsolete entries are removed.

Clear the three lint errors on the branch

Format a removal-refusal union, and build the getInfoAsync mock's FileInfo values as typed objects instead of asserting object literals.

Keep the lockfile's app version at 0.1.3

The previous commit set the app back to 0.1.3; bun.lock still named 0.1.4 and the next install would rewrite it.

Keep the app at 0.1.3 so merging does not publish a release

Merging to main runs the release when app.json's version is new. Set the app,
workspace and root versions back to 0.1.3 and regenerate the version artwork,
which now matches what main shipped byte for byte. The 0.1.4 release fixture
stays as the description of the next release: while the tree sits at a released
version, the completeness test lets the newest fixture claim only a later
version, and the strict checks return as soon as app.json is bumped.

Exempt held-out evaluation fixtures from the follow-up check

The evaluation cases quote FOLLOWUP(F41) and similar ids as fixtures of the checker itself, as its own test file does.

Record the first held-out evaluation run

Five trials over four cases from real Sovran history, all graded correct with no false block. F163 states why this cannot yet measure rates or compare models.

Keep the tampered test suite green in the held-out tampering case

In run v1 the tampered fixture kept assertions for removed code fixtures, so the suite failed 8 of 12 and the reviewer had a red run to point at. The case now removes those assertions too; a test holds every planted-defect workspace to a passing suite.

Add a held-out evaluation set built from real Sovran history

Four cases: a real crash fixed in edca4842b to implement from scratch; a guard
removal a reviewer proposed on PR #289 and live research refuted; a commit that
silences code references and trims the test that would catch it; and the clean
#289 fix as a false-block control. Workspaces hold only the case's history.
Graders are tested against the original bug, the recorded fix, a different valid
fix, a swallowed crash, and vague or wrong review verdicts.

Record the live coordinator restart and the remaining non-UTF-8 gap

A fresh coordinator recovered an in-flight worker from T3 lineage without a second dispatch; F157 records it. The recovered research confirmed that names that are not valid UTF-8 are still skipped, now F164.

Do not report a superseded required attempt as a check nobody requires

An earlier failed run of a required check counted as outside the requirements, so the readiness reason misnamed it and it could stand in for GitHub's UNSTABLE explanation. Match by required name instead.

Record the first live full-send task to reach ready

Task 4fc29087 produced PR #289 with Claude-only fallback while Codex was out of quota. F157 and F159 now list what that run established, the controller defects it exposed, and what is still unverified: the GPT side, a mid-task restart, Hunch app removal and the phone.

Disclose failing checks nobody requires instead of waiting on them

The first live PR stayed waiting because Hunch, a GitHub App check outside the
sealed and branch-required sets, failed on the base branch's config and GitHub
reported the PR as UNSTABLE. The owner decided Hunch runs locally, not in CI.
Ready now accepts UNSTABLE only when a non-required, non-passing check explains
it, and names those checks in the readiness reason. A ready task also reports
that reason instead of its last waiting message.

Identify a PR's head repository the way gh actually reports it

gh leaves headRepository.nameWithOwner empty for same-repository pull requests,
so the first live publication created its PR and then refused to recognise it.
Compare headRepositoryOwner.login and headRepository.name instead, and make the
fake gh in the publisher tests return the shape observed on that PR.

Clear a repair's failure reason once verification passes

A task already in review still reported 'Check failed', so status answered 'why is this blocked' wrongly. The journal keeps the reason.

Fail a baseline whose tampered submodule cannot be fingerprinted

A baseline test that wrote into, removed or replaced an empty submodule folder
made the post-run fingerprint throw, escaping verify before the worktree was
removed and leaving the command pending. Treat an unfingerprintable baseline as
changed, so the check fails and cleanup runs. Also match gitlink paths that
contain a newline.

Let regression baselines run in repositories with submodules

A baseline runs in a fresh detached worktree, where submodules stay empty. The
source fingerprint refuses an empty gitlink, so in this repository, with its
BitChat gitlinks, every regression baseline failed during setup with "Source
fingerprint unavailable" before any test ran. The baseline now records each
empty gitlink's pinned commit and fingerprints the rest. The shared source
fingerprint, used for native build stamps, is unchanged.

State in each brief the acceptance rules its schema cannot show

After three live research results were refused for unstated rules, a read-only
sweep listed the rest. Requirement ids, unique finding ids, per-path history
review, one proposal per obligation, review digests, oracle citations, the
scope of every evidence field, implementation's path and lockfile limits, and
read-only roles leaving the checkout unchanged are now in schema descriptions
or brief text. Validation is unchanged.

Tell workers a history owner is a file path

The brief's JSON Schema drops zod refinements, so owner appeared as any string.
A live research worker named the author there and its result was refused when
the controller read owner as a file at the base commit. Describe both history
path fields in the schema the brief carries.

Accept artifact inspections cited in the artifact: form

The brief tells workers to cite saved artifacts as artifact:<file>, but the
inspection checks compared only the bare packet path. A live research worker
cited the history snapshot the documented way, with the correct hash, and was
refused. Both checks now accept either spelling while still requiring the
packet's exact hash, and the brief states the rule.
Check every role's offered fields against the ownership table

Show each worker only the assessment fields its role may submit

Every brief carried the full assessment schema, where history, historyReview and
the resolution lists are optional, but the controller refuses each from all but
one role. A live research worker followed the schema, added the audit's
historyReview, and its otherwise complete result could not be accepted. Briefs
now carry a role-specific schema from one ownership table; the validators are
unchanged, so legacy tasks keep their behaviour.

Write the whole CLI result before exiting

Read through Python's subprocess capture, a large brief stopped after the first
64 KiB while the CLI still exited 0, so a coordinator could act on a partial
packet. Wait for stdout to accept the full result. Bun.write to stdout also
truncated and then hung in the same setup, so it is not used.

Let default research fall back across providers

Research listed only Luna and Sol, so a Codex outage ended every task before
intake, although the routing research names Opus 5.5 as the next research
fallback. Add it, and test that every default route keeps a candidate on each
provider.

Label the extra review from its current passing attempt

The PR disclosure named Claude whenever any submitted extra review in any
generation used Claude, even if a later generation's passing review was GPT.
Read it from the current passing reviews instead. Add the Claude-only case with
GPT-only off, which the audit-step change needed and no test covered. The
disclosure wording itself still has no test.

Defaults now seal allowClaudeOnly with Fable 5.1 as the second extra-review
candidate (from the previous commit), as the owner approved on 2026-10-16.

Allow approved Claude-only completion with an extra outside-author review

Codex quota can now block a task the same way Claude quota could. Mirror the
GPT-only rule: a routed policy may set allowClaudeOnly, and then a Claude model
outside every source-author model may take the extra review slot. Policies sealed
before the flag existed keep no such authority, and the PR disclosure names the
family that supplied the extra review.
Record live proof that failed captures fail their step

Keep a step failed until its picture is retained

A failed checkpoint capture after passing assertions left the step marked ok with no
picture; only the run-level failure named it. Record the step as failed until its
image and screen map are written. Record the three clean fresh-capture iOS runs and
the obstructed-screenshot rejection in F156.

Capture current simulator screens instead of cached frames

Use fresh simctl captures and decoded image samples for checkpoints and bounded settling. Remove the addon watcher and its restart protocol. Retain acquisition intervals and qualify sampled observations in the evidence viewer; continuous video remains separate evidence.
Reject incomplete story recordings and bound cleanup
Record public iOS binding proof and recorder gap
Bind fresh iOS stories to selected and installed builds
Record native story proof and remaining controller boundaries
Require onboarding as the legal story destination
Run bundled Android stories through owned emulator sessions

Bind native build stamps to stable source inputs

Reject source drift during compilation and bundled caches without source evidence. Force Android JavaScript bundling when rebuilding so sibling workspace changes cannot reuse stale Gradle outputs.

Build isolated Android bundled story apps

Select the Release test network policy explicitly, bind build fingerprints to the mode, and sanitize inherited fixture controls. Preserve ordinary Release policy and mode-aware bundle caching. Native controller certification remains incomplete.
Keep harness schema details private to their modules
Run harness tests before competing workspace suites
Record a no-change development evaluation and grader calibration
Run harness checks on stacked PRs with a declared test runtime
Reject test runtimes that ignore expected-failure semantics
Separate historical harness findings from remaining validation work
Wait for the current splash before native story input and assertions
Retain Android story diagnostics before owned emulator teardown
Keep large task references in verified snapshots instead of every prompt
Normalize Android full-window control coordinates before native taps
Require enabled legal controls after agreement actions
Read development React roots without replacing the DevTools hook
Measure native response latency separately from capture polling
Require an observed window before native screen assertions pass

Run fresh Android stories with installed payload and session evidence

Reuse the owned emulator lifecycle and shared story player/results. Keep native certification blocked: real Android probes expose the development hook capture gap and startup deadline failure.
Include nested component test directories in task context

Route task context from planned files and current native decisions

Keep existing declared and inferred safety gates while choosing guidance from pre-edit planned paths. Include companion conventions, both native testing decisions, Android flow rationale and versioned component-test guidance, including new hook tests. Refuse ambiguous RNTL major declarations rather than silently choosing an incompatible reference.

Retain sealed context on restart; ask research and audit to classify active and deleted follow-ups in the existing evidence fields. Validated the full harness suite before review fixes, targeted regressions after fixes, and harness type checks. Context remains substantial; this change corrects relevance and omissions rather than claiming a prompt-size reduction.

Bind story log sessions and finalize evidence after cleanup

Require the expected run and platform before accepting socket evidence or replaying pending requests. Preserve profile restart support and retain every received log entry outside step windows. Each play has a unique identity, and setup reports cannot remain green when cleanup or log retention fails.

Validated with 85 focused tests, real WebSocket regressions that fail on the parent, root type checks, native scenario validation, an ordinary disposable iOS story and a deliberate log-retention failure after all five UI assertions passed. Native binary/controller binding and Android story proof remain open. Record the real provider quota failure without claiming a live PR.
Require meaningful regression comparisons and independent test judgments
Keep checks with unknown publisher identity unverified
Require workflow identity before accepting GitHub Actions checks
Verify sealed and server CI requirements against raw GitHub check identities

fix(e2e): the app is not called still while a page that has just appeared may yet slide in

With four simulators running, a new page was in the tree 176 ms before
its native slide began. The screen was called still in that gap, and the
next tap landed on a page that was moving: the commonest failure of the
first parallel run of thirteen stories.

The app now counts itself as moving for up to a second after a page
appears, or after a page change is asked for, until the slide starts and
then ends. A page that appears in place (a tab) costs that second once.

The page-change request is logged as nav.action. In the bundled test
build that entry never appears, so the page's own appearance is what
holds in practice; why the request is not seen there is not yet known.
